scenario: WIBTA if I told my cousin his kid can’t stay in our house? | My cousin (M27) recently moved in with my husband and I. We completely closed of the very large main bedroom and bathroom to create a flatlet for him that’s separate from the house with his own entrance so it’s basically two separate units of one house. Now my cousin has a 2 year old and he’s busy with a custody battle with his ex so he can get to spend more time with his son. I completely support this and really hopes he gets more time with his son. Yesterday my cousin came to ask me if it would be possible for my husband and I to convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son if and when he comes to visit over weekends. There is no access from my cousin’s room into our part of the house and he doesn’t have keys to come and go as he pleases. I understand that the court will be looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him (and to be honest his current room and bathroom is more than big enough) but I’m not comfortable with letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin has no access to him and I’m not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that’s just the way my family is and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. WIBTA for telling him I will not allow his son to sleep in our house and completely jeopardizing his court case?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my cousin that his kid can't stay in our house. Let me break this down step by step. First, my cousin moved in with my husband and me. We converted the main bedroom and bathroom into a separate flatlet for him, so he has his own entrance. That means our living spaces are completely separate. He has a 2-year-old son, and he's going through a custody battle with his ex. I support him because I want him to spend more time with his son. Yesterday, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son when he comes over weekends. But here's the thing: there's no access from my cousin's room into our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. I'm not comfortable letting his son stay in our house because my cousin can't access him, and I don't want to take responsibility for his kid. The family is really involved in this, and everyone expects me to help my cousin with his custody situation. If I say no, it might jeopardize his court case because the court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son. Honestly, his current room and bathroom are more than big enough, but I'm still not okay with letting his son stay in our house. So, is it right or wrong for me to tell him no? I'm confused because I want to support him, but I also have my own boundaries and responsibilities. I don't want to put myself in a position where I'm responsible for his child, especially since he can't access the house freely. But on the other hand, helping him could really make a difference in his custody case, and the family expects me to help. I'm also thinking about the Islamic perspective. In Islam, family ties are very important, and helping relatives is encouraged. But there's also the aspect of personal boundaries and not taking on responsibilities that you're not comfortable with. I need to balance these two aspects. Maybe I should consider alternative solutions. Is there another way to help my cousin without letting his son stay in our house? Could we provide some other form of support? Or perhaps suggest that he finds another place that meets the court's requirements? I'm also wondering about the legal implications. If the court sees that he has a suitable space, it might help his case. But if I refuse, it might look bad on him, even though the space is sufficient. I don't want to be the reason he loses custody. On the other hand, I have to think about my own peace of mind and the safety of my home. If I'm not comfortable with his son staying here, then maybe it's better to find another solution. Maybe I can talk to him and explain my concerns, and together we can find a way that works for everyone. I'm also considering the impact on our family relationship. If I say no, will that strain our relationship? I don't want that, but I also don't want to compromise my own boundaries. In the end, I think it's important to communicate openly with my cousin. Let him know my concerns and see if we can find a middle ground. If not, then I have to make the decision that's best for me and my family, even if it's hard.
